verification.note: Reproduced by tracing the code. frontend/src/components/appshell/folderPosition.ts:70 decides link = strictAncestor && !sameFolders(narrowFolders(targetFolders, folder), targetFolders). It compares the crumb's view with the target's top, not with the current view narrowFolders(targetFolders, position), which is the value LibraryFace uses for its requests (readingapp/LibraryFace.tsx:117-125, videoapp/LibraryFace.tsx:125). narrowFolders (appshell/folders.ts:26-40) keeps a target folder that lies inside the chosen folder and drops one that does not. Take target folders [A/b/c, Q] and position A/b. Crumb A: it is a strict ancestor, and narrowFolders(T, A) = [A/b/c], which is not equal to T, so A is a link. The current view is narrowFolders(T, A/b) = [A/b/c], so A leads to the same view. The trail ends at the base A/b/c, because the backend's _folder_base (backend/app/routers/shelves.py:191-208) descends while there is a single child, and A/b/c starts with A/b/. The same happens at position A/b/c, where both A and A/b are same-view links. Reachability: following chips from the top (base '', chips A and Q, then base A/b/c with chips under it) never lands on A/b or A/b/c. So this case needs a hand-written or bookmarked `folder` URL. At deeper positions reached by chips (for example A/b/c/d), the crumbs A, A/b and A/b/c all lead to [A/b/c]. That differs from the current view, so I8 holds there, though the three links all lead to the same view.

specification_compliance: I8 (r6), the folder crumb clause: violated when the position is a folder whose narrowed folder set equals an ancestor's narrowed folder set (for example target [A/b/c, Q] at position A/b). The crumb test at folderPosition.ts:70 compares against the target's top, not the current view.
potential_unspecified_behavior: Under a folder-limited target, several ancestor crumbs (for example A, A/b, A/b/c) can each be links to the same view. I8 does not forbid this as long as that view differs from the current one.
regression_risks: Changing the crumb test to compare against narrowFolders(targetFolders, position) would turn a crumb's link into plain text whenever it leads to the current view. Existing crumb tests that expect links under folder-limited targets would need review.
test_coverage: I found no test in appshell/__tests__ that covers folderCrumbs with a multi-folder target and a position whose narrowed set equals an ancestor's narrowed set. I checked only by grep, not with a full read of the test files.
not_verified: Did not run any tests or the app; the reproduction is by code tracing only.
